description: This bar chart illustrates the number of datasets categorized as either “Targeted” or “Untargeted” by year, from 2012 to 2022, with the vertical axis labeled “Number of datasets” ranging from 0 to 160 in increments of 20, and the horizontal axis labeled “Year” displaying the years in chronological order. Each year is represented by a stacked bar, where the lower blue segment corresponds to “Untargeted” datasets and the upper orange segment corresponds to “Targeted” datasets, as indicated by the legend. The values for each segment are approximate: for instance, in 2012, the “Untargeted” bar is approximately 1 dataset and the “Targeted” bar is approximately 0.5 datasets, totaling roughly 1.5 datasets; in 2016, the “Untargeted” segment is approximately 2 datasets and the “Targeted” segment is approximately 6 datasets; in 2017, the “Untargeted” segment is approximately 10 datasets and the “Targeted” segment is approximately 15 datasets; in 2018, the “Untargeted” segment is approximately 15 datasets and the “Targeted” segment is approximately 25 datasets; in 2019, the “Untargeted” segment is approximately 15 datasets and the “Targeted” segment is approximately 45 datasets; in 2020, the “Untargeted” segment is approximately 45 datasets and the “Targeted” segment is approximately 80 datasets; in 2021, the “Untargeted” segment is approximately 65 datasets and the “Targeted” segment is approximately 95 datasets; and in 2022, the “Untargeted” segment is approximately 5 datasets and the “Targeted” segment is approximately 25 datasets. The bars are not sorted, but are presented chronologically along the x-axis. The chart visually emphasizes the growing dominance of “Targeted” datasets over time, with the “Targeted” segment becoming significantly larger in later years, particularly peaking in 2021 at approximately 95 datasets. The data for 2022 is noted in the caption as being only partially available.
